question:
I have a model called "stg_skills" that I run and then perform dbt test --model.

The next model is "dwh_skills".

Let's say the table "stg_skills" has 1,000 rows and 990 of them passed all tests, how do I populate the "dwh_skills" with those 990 good rows?

Thanks.
title: DBT tests - moving "good" rows to the next table
answer:
If you perform dbt run + dbt test, you will not prevent downstream models to be populated with data that did not pass tests: you are just running evertything, and then checking tests on all the ran models.

On the other hand, though, you can also use dbt build. With this command, "tests on upstream resources will block downstream resources from running, and a test failure will cause those downstream resources to skip entirely" (see docs here), meaning that if there's a breaking test in stg_skills, dwh_skills will not be built until that error is fixed.

In my opinion, that's the closest you can get. I believe there's no way to just run those rows where the tests passed - it is either all or nothing.
